title: On Selling the field to the man from town
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：sell　|　正文 363 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sell 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the gardener ① sold the field to the man from town in the rain, and every apprentice in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three springs on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the gardener ② sells the field to the man from town without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ sell the field to the man from town at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ sold the field to the man from town before — a line in the notebook for April 1972 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Selling the field to the man from town in the rain, the gardener said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ sell at twice what it cost without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Sell at twice what it cost at once and never mention it again.

By 1985 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the notebook, and a new apprentice from the next garden ⑧ sells at twice what it cost in the rain every spring without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bed, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ sold the field to the man from town again when nobody else would.

⑩ To sell the field to the man from town, my mother said in 1990, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody sells the field to the man from town without complaint again and somebody must sell the field to the man from town in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 出售（一般过去式 sold the field to the man from town：1978 年园丁头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 出售（一般现在 sells the field to the man from town：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 出售（不定式 to sell the field to the man from town：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 出售（过去完成时 had sold the field to the man from town：1972 年四月的园艺笔记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 出售（动名词 selling the field to the man from town 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 卖出（sell at twice what it cost：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去卖出卖到原价的两倍）
G. v. 卖出（sell at twice what it cost：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 出售（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 sells at twice what it cost，而母亲又一次 sold the field to the man from town）

answers.why: sell 意为“出售”，1978 年园丁淋着雨出售把那块地卖给了城里人，那是园子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 sold。
sell 意为“出售”，自那以后园丁毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 sells。
sell 意为“出售”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯出售把那块地卖给了城里人”，此处为不定式 to sell the field to the man from town。
sell 意为“出售”，园艺笔记里 四月 那行字说明早在 1985 年之前就有人出售过，故用过去完成时 had sold。
sell 意为“出售”，园丁说“出售把那块地卖给了城里人这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 selling the field to the man from town 作主语。
sell 意为“卖出”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去卖出卖到原价的两倍”，should ever 之后用原形 sell at twice what it cost。
sell 意为“卖出”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻卖出卖到原价的两倍（sell at twice what it cost at once），以后再也不要提起。
sell 意为“出售”，新来的学徒每个春天都照例卖出卖到原价的两倍，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 sells。
sell 意为“出售”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨出售把那块地卖给了城里人，用一般过去式 sold 叙述。
sell 意为“出售”，结尾那句是母亲 1990 年的话：要出售把那块地卖给了城里人，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和园子记住的那一件。

items: 1978 年，园丁淋着雨出售把那块地卖给了城里人；园子里每一个学徒都说这是头一回。（sold the field to the man from town）
多年以后，园丁仍毫无怨言地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（sells the field to the man from town）

早在 1972 年就有人出售把那块地卖给了城里人，四月那天园艺笔记上的一行字就是证据。（had sold the field to the man from town）
园丁说过，淋着雨出售把那块地卖给了城里人这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（selling the field to the man from town 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻卖出卖到原价的两倍，以后再也不要提起。（sell at twice what it cost，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sell 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1978 the gardener sold the field to the man from town in the rain, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the gardener sells the field to the man from town without complaint whenever the garden asks.
Selling the field to the man from town in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever sell at twice what it cost without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next garden sells at twice what it cost in the rain every spring, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother sold the field to the man from town again, and the garden remembered that half.
